## Findings
- claim-1: \(\Lambda/I_{r,q}\) has the integral Schur basis indexed by \(\lambda\subseteq q^r\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 213-218]
- claim-2: The antipode identity is \(S(s_\lambda)=(-1)^{|\lambda|}s_{\lambda'}\), yielding \(\sum_{\alpha,\beta}(-1)^{|\alpha|}c_{\alpha,\beta}^{\rho}s_{\alpha'}s_\beta=0\) for \(\rho\ne\varnothing\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 702-735]
- claim-3: Assume \(a+j\le r,\ a+i\le q,\ b\le i,j\). For every \(\rho\subseteq b^a\), \[ [\bar s_{(i^j,\rho)}] =(-1)^{|\rho|} [\bar s_{(i+\rho'_1,\ldots,i+\rho'_b,i^{j-b})}] \quad\text{in }Q=J_v/A_+J_v. \]
## Strategy
Let \(q=n-r\), \(A=\Lambda/I_{r,q}\), and \(Q=J_v/A_+J_v\). Pad \(\rho=(\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_a)\subseteq b^a\) by zeros and set
\[
\rho'_k=\#\{\ell:\rho_\ell\ge k\}\quad(1\le k\le b).
\]
The intended statement is
\[
[\bar s_{(i^j,\rho)}]
=(-1)^{|\rho|}
[\bar s_{(i+\rho'_1,\ldots,i+\rho'_b,i^{j-b})}]
\quad\text{in }Q. \tag{E}
\]
Here zero parts and \(i^0\) are omitted. The proposed stronger identity in \(\Lambda\) is
\[
s_{(i^j,\rho)}-(-1)^{|\rho|}s_{(i+\rho'_1,\ldots,i+\rho'_b,i^{j-b})}
=\sum_{\sigma\subsetneq\rho}
(-1)^{|\rho|-|\sigma|+1}\omega(s_{\rho/\sigma})s_{(i^j,\sigma)}. \tag{R}
\]
Thus
\[
F_{\rho,\sigma}=(-1)^{|\rho|-|\sigma|+1}\omega(s_{\rho/\sigma})
\in\Lambda_{|\rho|-|\sigma|}.
\]
If (R) were proved, projection to \(A\) would put its right side in \(A_+J_v\), proving (E). For \(\rho=\varnothing\), including \(a=0\), (E) is tautological.

## Gaps
The required determinant/rectangle-attachment proof of (R) is still missing. The supplied Hopf identity
\[
\sum_{\lambda,\mu}(-1)^{|\lambda|}c_{\lambda,\mu}^{\rho}
s_{\lambda'}s_\mu=0
\]
does not itself yield (R): no verified linear map from its full-coordinate terms or from the accepted \(\operatorname{Lin}_\varphi\)-row relation to the products
\(\omega(s_{\rho/\sigma})s_{(i^j,\sigma)}\) has been supplied.

In particular, no Jacobi--Trudi or complementary-minor computation has established the endpoint coefficient
\(-(-1)^{|\rho|}\), the cancellation of all other terms, or the claimed indexing by exactly \(\sigma\subsetneq\rho\). The graded-kernel presentation proves lower-family independence but supplies no coordinates for the right-adjoined class. No admissible counterexample is provided.

Therefore this certificate is **not established**.

## Next
Supply either:

1. a complete Jacobi--Trudi/Cauchy--Binet proof of (R), with explicit matrices, minor bijection, and Laplace signs; or  
2. an admissible parameter counterexample to (E) with exact Schur-coordinate data.
